title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Tuning for the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing behavior, enforce fairness across request priorities, prevent starvation of small/low-latency requests, and add robust timeout/lease handling so stuck requests don't block KV cache / batch slots. Motivation: In production we observed that optimizing purely for throughput caused head-of-line and starvation scenarios: long-sequence or high-token requests would occupy effective batch slots and KV cache state leading to elevated p95/p99 queue times for small interactive requests. This change rebalances throughput/latency tradeoffs with low-risk controls and observability. Implementation: 1) Per-priority FIFO sub-queues with a configurable fairness window and aging multiplier so lower-priority requests accrue effective weight over time; 2) Starvation prevention: requests that exceed starvation_threshold_ms are eligible for preemptive dequeueing and forced batching in a dedicated fairness bucket; 3) Lease/slot timeouts: a per-request slot lease (slot_lease_ms) ensures a batch slot held by a hung worker is reclaimed; we added a soft-kill path that cancels long-waiting KV-cache reservations and triggers a fast-fallback variant; 4) Adaptive max_batch_delay_ms: batch delay is tuned based on realtime queue depth heuristics so we dynamically balance batching efficiency vs latency SLOs; 5) KV cache coalescing improvements: avoid locking KV cache for requests that will be preempted due to starvation handling; 6) New metrics and traces: batching.queue_time_p50/p95/p99, batching.fairness_skew, scheduler.starvation_count, scheduler.reclaimed_lease_count, kvcache.contention_count. Tests and validation: unit tests for scheduler invariants and simulated workloads were added under continuous_batcher/tests, e2e perf harness runs against the perf lab show p99 queue time for interactive workload decreased by ~2.3x while aggregate throughput drop is <1.5% on average. We included CI perf benchmarks and a canary rollout plan behind a feature flag. Rollout and risk: feature gated behind feature_flag.continuous_batcher_v2; started gradual rollout to 10% of traffic, monitored metrics for 48h then 50% and full. Rollback: feature flag toggle and automatic fallback to previous scheduling policy if scheduler.reclaimed_lease_count spikes or per-route latency SLOs degrade beyond configured thresholds. Backwards compatibility and migration: no model or API surface change; config knobs added with sane defaults matching previous behavior. Notes: this PR touches core scheduler and requires staged rollout/coordination with infra; see linked Linear tickets for followups.
